editorial.brief: A PHP vulnerability is the one story that shows up in several feeds: PHP2Shell drew 238,212 Wikipedia views, a Hacker News thread reached 322 points, and a Mastodon user observed that 70 percent of the internet needs fixing. GitLab's critical patch release added 289 points. Wikipedia's actual leader, Jailer 2, arrived with 278,796 views and no explanation.
editorial.cover_sub: Jailer 2 took 278,796 Wikipedia views on a day when the feeds were busy with a PHP flaw, and not one of them offered a reason for it.
editorial.wiki_deck: Jailer 2 led Wikipedia with 278,796 views, 1.2 times the runner-up. Nothing else in the snapshot says why.
editorial.letter_headline: A PHP flaw runs through the feeds
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is anxious about PHP, GitLab and an integer multiplication paper. Lemmy is earnest about science and cars. Bluesky is angry and celebratory in several languages. Mastodon is angry too, and also tending a chicken.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire ran on AI: a $100 million US STEM pledge, a McDonald's pricing suit, and thin entry-level hiring in India. Searchers there looked up Sensex, HDFC Securities and Mathrubhumi.
editorial.markets_deck: Five markets at $1M each. The Iran ceasefire holding is 95 percent; a Republican sweep is 9 percent; a Fed hike, Tim Scott and Kings-Clippers sit at zero.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,205,009 players, Dota 2 at 907,099 and PUBG at 778,436. On Twitch, caseoh_ led with 61,267 viewers. Call of Duty appears on both Steam and YouTube.
editorial.yt_headline: A tribute to Santa Fe Klan
editorial.yt_note: Santa Fe Klan's tribute leads with 1,723,676 views, then a casino warning at 1,195,530 and Honest Trailers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day at 879,841. The Rings of Power season 3 trailer has 542,695.
editorial.closing_note: Gone by tomorrow's edition: Jailer 2's lead of 40,584 views, the 322-point PHP thread, the 95 percent ceasefire market that ends with today's date, and caseoh_'s 61,267 viewers. The chicken, presumably, stays indoors.
wiki_paras: Jailer 2 led Wikipedia's most-read list with 278,796 views. The data does not say what it is or why people went looking, and no other feed mentions it. It is the day's leading mystery, supplied with a number and nothing else.

The margin was modest. PHP2Shell took second place with 238,212 views, a gap of 40,584, which works out at a lead of 1.2 times. Elizabeth Holmes had 208,412, the Aberfan disaster 187,692 and Heath Ledger 177,482. Five articles span about 101,000 views from first to last.

The runner-up is the one with company. PHP2Shell sits beside a Hacker News thread on a PHP vulnerability at 322 points and a Mastodon post about 70 percent of the internet needing a fix. The cover subject stands alone, while the second-place story is argued over everywhere else.
letter_paras: The snapshot found a day with one loud subject and a mystery on top. A PHP vulnerability turns up in Wikipedia, Hacker News and Mastodon at once, with GitLab's critical patch release at 289 points as a neighbour. Meanwhile Jailer 2 leads Wikipedia unexplained. The rest is scattered, as usual.

The quiet corners did better. A Mastodon user reports that a lonesome chicken is now an indoor pet and has learned from the cats to guard the home. Bluesky posted a Painted Bunting. The USGS logged 25 quakes of M2.5 or more, the largest an M5.3 near Reykjanes Ridge.

A snapshot taken in one minute settles an argument that rolling feeds blur: whether two things are the same event. A PHP flaw on Hacker News and a PHP page on Wikipedia, seen together, are one story. Seen a day apart, they are two coincidences. Simultaneity is the cheapest evidence a small desk can buy.
